subject: URGENT: Production 5xx/429 surge — VPC peering route churn and DNS drift
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: oncall@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: URGENT: Production 5xx/429 surge — VPC peering route churn and DNS drift

Team —

We just saw a sudden, correlated spike in 5xx and 429 responses for FinTechCo (us-east-1). Error rate jumped from ~0.5% to ~18% at 09:06 PST and has continued to oscillate. Latency SLOs are violated for multiple routes (primary model inference and embedding endpoints).

Initial signals:
- 5xx/429 correlated with elevated RTT and connection timeouts to the customer-dedicated pool.
- Control-plane metrics show repeated BGP/peering route flaps between our Dedicated cluster and the FinTechCo VPC starting ~09:02.
- DNS resolution for the customer's service endpoints intermittently returned old/private IPs for a subset of calls.

I attached a short packet capture and the support bundle. I suspect a peering route churn combined with stale DNS entries in the customer's NAT/firewall path is causing request retries and queueing at the edge (retry amplification).

Immediate asks:
1) Monica / Marissa: loop FinTechCo account team & Cx (Lisa) now and coordinate an exec sync if the impact continues.
2) Oncall: collect additional pcap + service logs and increase sampling on tail latencies for the affected routes.
3) Laura / Rishi: check if any dedicated NAT gateways or firewall rules were recently changed for this tenant on our side; confirm our egress path stability.

I'll stand up a short bridge (details in Jira INF-7832).

Attachments: packet_capture.pcap (pcap), support_bundle_20261222.tar.gz (logs), vpc_topology_sketch.png

— Jonas
Senior Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Marissa: please prepare an incident summary we can share with the customer execs if this persists beyond the next hour.

— Monica (CSM)
From: Lisa Nguyen <lisa.nguyen@fintechco.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: devops@fintechco.com, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 09:37:12 -0800
Subject: Re: URGENT: Production 5xx/429 surge — VPC peering route churn and DNS drift

Monica / Jonas —

We see a flurry of route withdraws on our side as well. Our edge team reports that a maintenance job rolled out an iptables rewrite to outbound NAT rules at 09:01 PST (automated job). They rolled it back at 09:14 but the symptoms persisted for a while because several long-lived NAT mappings kept routing to decommissioned IPs.

We are collecting NAT table snapshots and will share them to the bridge. Attaching their initial NAT dump and a short traceroute output.

— Lisa
Network Lead, FinTechCo
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 10:02:45 -0800
Subject: Re: URGENT: Production 5xx/429 surge — VPC peering route churn and DNS drift

Quick update from infra: we confirmed no planned changes on Redwood's dedicated NAT/GW in us-east-1 during that window. However, our telemetry shows sustained connection timeouts to the FinTechCo peered CIDR from 09:02–09:22 with occasional recovery windows where traffic drains and then backs up again.

Actions taken:
- Increased connection timeout thresholds on the front-door for the tenant to avoid harsh 5xxs from transient DNS mismatches.
- Flushed our local DNS cache for the cluster nodes serving that tenant and forced a fresh resolution path.
- Collected additional tcpdump slices (uploaded to drive).

Hypothesis: combined effect of (A) external NAT rollback leaving stale mappings, (B) BGP withdraw/announce churn causing asymmetric paths, and (C) client retries amplifying queue depth at our edge. Need FinTechCo to confirm NAT table convergence and also to ensure their route advertisements have stabilized.

— Rishi (Infra)
From: AWS Support <aws-support@amazon.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, lisa.nguyen@fintechco.com
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 13:11:33 -0800
Subject: RE: Observed peering flaps — case 123456

Hi team —

We reviewed the peering session metrics for the timeframe you provided. We observed repeated route withdraws originating from a customer-side edge device effecting the peering connection. The withdraws correlate with an automated job detected on the customer's VPC (we can see the same timeline Lisa reported). AWS recommends:
1) confirm BGP timers on the customer's router to reduce flap sensitivity during maintenance windows,
2) ensure route withdrawal is coordinated with any NAT reassignments so connections are quiesced,
3) provide us packet captures/traces and we will open a deeper infrastructure-level investigation if flaps continue.

We have appended our support case notes to your ticket: https://support.aws.amazon.com/case/123456

— AWS Support Engineer
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, lisa.nguyen@fintechco.com, aws-support@amazon.com, mike@cloudpartner.io
Date: Wed, 23 Dec 2026 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Summary & exec next steps — FinTechCo incident (INF-7832)

Folks — thank you for the quick responses. Short summary for execs and next steps we agreed on the bridge:

Summary: transient peering route churn + a FinTechCo automated NAT rewrite at 09:01 PST resulted in stale NAT mappings and intermittent DNS resolution of internal IPs. The combination produced retry amplification and queueing at our edge, manifesting as elevated 5xx/429 rates between 09:02–09:40.

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA):
- FinTechCo: confirm NAT table convergence and BGP timer adjustments (Lisa / DevOps) — within 2 hours of this note.
- Redwood Infra: continue increased sampling and provide post-incident pcap + tail-latency histogram (Rishi / Jonas) — EOD today.
- Security/Compliance: collect audit trail for outbound connections during the incident window for customer audit (Laura) — 24h.
- Customer success / Account: prepare customer-facing incident report and draft credit proposal if SLA breach confirmed (Monica / Marissa) — 48h.

Marissa: please escalate to our leadership chain (SOC/Head of Platform) if FINTECH execs request immediate credits or an exec briefing. I'll prepare a one-pager and proposed remediation timeline after the infra artifacts land.

Attachments: incident-digest-draft.md (internal), link to pcap and logs provided in Jira.

— Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
